questions.stem: Which service provides object storage for virtually any amount of data, accessed through web APIs?

options.rationale: S3 stores objects in buckets and is accessed over HTTPS APIs.
EBS provides block volumes for EC2.
EFS provides a shared file system.
Instance store is temporary block storage on the host.

questions.explanation: Object storage (S3), block storage (EBS, instance store) and file storage (EFS, FSx) are the three storage types.

questions.stem: Which service provides block storage volumes that attach to Amazon EC2 instances and keep their data independently of the instance's life?

options.rationale: Instance store data is lost when the instance stops or terminates.
Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes persist independently and can be detached and reattached.
S3 is object storage, not a volume.
Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a shared file system, not a block volume.

questions.explanation: The clues are block volumes and data that outlives the instance: EBS fits both, while instance store is block storage that is lost and EFS is file storage.

questions.stem: Which statement about Amazon EC2 instance store is correct?

options.text: It persists after the instance is terminated
options.rationale: Instance store does not persist after termination.

options.text: It can be detached and moved to a different instance
options.rationale: Instance store is tied to the host and cannot be moved between instances.

options.text: Its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates
options.rationale: Instance store is temporary storage on disks physically attached to the host.

options.text: It is a backup copy that AWS stores as an Amazon EBS snapshot
options.rationale: EBS snapshots are backups of EBS volumes; instance store is a disk on the host.

questions.explanation: The clue is temporary storage on the host: instance store suits buffers, caches and scratch data, while Amazon EBS volumes keep their data when an instance stops.

questions.stem: Which service provides a managed file system that many Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances can mount at the same time?

options.rationale: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes are block storage, typically attached to one instance.
Instance store is local to one instance.
Deep Archive is for long-term archives.
Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a serverless, elastic NFS file system that many instances can share.

questions.explanation: The clue is many instances mounting the same file system: EFS is shared file storage, while an EBS volume is block storage usually attached to one instance.

questions.stem: A company needs a fully managed file server that supports the SMB protocol for its Windows applications. Which service should it use?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
options.rationale: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed Windows file storage over SMB.
EFS uses NFS and is aimed at Linux workloads.
EBS is block storage, not a managed file server.
Glacier is archival storage.

questions.explanation: The clue is SMB for Windows applications: FSx for Windows File Server is a managed Windows file server, while EFS serves Linux workloads over NFS.

questions.stem: Which service gives on-premises applications access to virtually unlimited cloud storage while caching frequently used data locally?

options.rationale: Direct Connect is a network link, not storage.
Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service with local caching.
EFS is a cloud file system without an on-premises cache appliance.
AWS Backup manages backups.

questions.explanation: Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage such as S3, with low-latency local access.

questions.stem: Which Amazon S3 storage class automatically moves objects between access tiers when access patterns change?

options.rationale: S3 Standard does not move objects between tiers.
Deep Archive is the lowest-cost archive class; it does not tier automatically.
Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and moves objects between tiers automatically.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ; it does not move objects.

questions.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering is a good choice when access patterns are unknown or change over time.

questions.stem: Which Amazon S3 storage class has the lowest storage cost and is meant for long-term archives that are rarely accessed and can wait hours for retrieval?

options.rationale: S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data.
Intelligent-Tiering optimizes cost for changing access patterns.
Standard-IA offers millisecond access at a higher storage price than Deep Archive.
Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class, with retrieval in hours.

questions.explanation: Classes trade storage price against access speed and retrieval cost.

questions.stem: How can a company automatically move Amazon S3 objects to a lower-cost storage class 90 days after they are created?

options.rationale: Lifecycle rules transition or expire objects automatically based on age.

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket
options.rationale: Versioning keeps object versions; it does not change storage classes.

options.text: Attach an IAM policy to the bucket owner
options.rationale: IAM policies control permissions.
Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads over long distances.

questions.explanation: Lifecycle policies reduce storage cost by moving older data to cheaper classes or deleting it.

questions.stem: Which service centrally manages and automates backups across AWS services such as Amazon EBS, Amazon RDS and Amazon EFS?

options.rationale: Storage Gateway provides hybrid access to cloud storage.
AWS Backup centralizes and automates data protection across AWS services.
Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads to S3.
AWS Config tracks configurations, not backups.

questions.explanation: AWS Backup uses backup plans to schedule and retain backups in one place.

questions.stem: A company needs storage for Amazon EC2 instances that keeps its data after the instances stop. Which TWO services meet this need? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Instance store data is lost when the instance stops.
ElastiCache is a managed caching service for applications, not storage that instances keep files or volumes on.
Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is persistent shared file storage.
CloudFront is a content delivery network.
Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes persist independently of the instance.

questions.explanation: The clue is keeping data after the instance stops: EBS volumes and EFS file systems are stored apart from the instance, while instance store lives on the host and loses its data.

questions.stem: Where are Amazon EBS snapshots stored?

options.text: In Amazon S3, managed by AWS
options.rationale: Snapshots are incremental backups that AWS stores in Amazon S3.

options.text: On the instance store of the instance
options.rationale: Instance store is temporary local storage.

options.text: On the same EBS volume they were taken from
options.rationale: Snapshots are stored separately from the volume.

options.text: In a bucket you create and manage yourself
options.rationale: Snapshots are not stored in your own S3 buckets.

questions.explanation: Snapshots can be used to create new volumes, copy data across Regions and back up volumes.

questions.stem: Which service continuously replicates on-premises or cloud servers to AWS so they can be recovered quickly after a disaster?

options.rationale: Storage Gateway provides hybrid access to cloud storage.
Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers and launches recovery instances on AWS when needed.
CloudFront delivers content.
EFS is a shared file system.

questions.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery reduces recovery time and the cost of idle standby infrastructure.
